NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a coordinated thermal-mechanical duty schedule — a two-stage ramp profile combined with support-proximal load placement and reduced soak temperature — that simultaneously minimizes the creep driving force (stress × time-at-temperature) on molybdenum rails and graphite felt. Standard practice treats ramp rate, soak temperature, load placement, and load mass as independent setpoints; the mitigation departs by co-optimizing them as a single schedule: (1) a slow initial ramp (2°C/min) through 800–1100°C where molybdenum creep initiates but stress relaxation occurs, then standard ramp above; (2) soak temperature reduced by 15°C (1235°C vs 1250°C) with unchanged soak duration; (3) loads placed within 10% of rail span from supports (vs centered) to cut bending moment by ~80%; (4) maximum load mass per rail span reduced by 20%. Adjacent-technique clearance: semiconductor annealing uses multi-stage ramps for stress control, but not coordinated with mechanical load-path optimization on creep-prone supports; vacuum brazing practice holds fixed ramps and centered loading. The mechanism attacks the failure physics by reducing the Larson-Miller parameter (time-temperature integral) and the applied stress simultaneously, where standard practice only limits peak temperature.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Molybdenum creep strain rate ε̇ = Aσⁿexp(-Q/RT) with n≈3–5, Q≈500–600 kJ/mol. Graphite felt sag follows similar time-temperature-stress dependence. Integrated creep strain Δε ∝ σⁿ × t × exp(-Q/RT).
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = creep driving force (σⁿ × t × exp(-Q/RT)); the mechanism moves it DOWN by: (a) reducing σ via support-proximal placement (bending moment ∝ distance from support, ~80% reduction at 10% span) and 20% mass reduction (σ ∝ load); (b) reducing T by 15°C at soak (exp(-Q/R·1500K) → ~35% rate reduction for Q=550 kJ/mol); (c) slow ramp through 800–1100°C allows stress relaxation without accumulating high-temperature creep time. Magnitude verification: combined effect ≈ (0.8)⁴ × 0.35 × (relaxation benefit) ≈ 0.14× baseline creep per cycle — a 7× reduction. This reduces rail deflection and felt sag accumulation per cycle, directly mitigating the failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| Row | Component / Operation | Class | Tag | Location / Parameter |
|-----|----------------------|-------|-----|---------------------|
| 1 | Furnace temperature controller recipe | Existing equipment | (a) | Stated furnace control system |
| 2 | Ramp profile: 2°C/min from RT to 800°C; 2°C/min from 800°C to 1100°C; standard ramp (e.g., 10°C/min) 1100°C to soak | Parameter change on (1) | (c) | Controller setpoint recipe |
| 3 | Soak temperature setpoint: 1235°C (vs 1250°C baseline) | Parameter change on (1) | (c) | Controller setpoint recipe |
| 4 | Soak duration: unchanged from baseline | Parameter change on (1) | (c) | Controller setpoint recipe |
| 5 | Load placement procedure: parts fixtured within 10% of rail span from nearest support | Procedure change | (c) | Load fixture / operator instruction |
| 6 | Load mass limit: ≤80% of baseline max mass per rail span | Procedure change | (c) | Load planning / operator instruction |
| 7 | Support inspection interval: unchanged (detection not prevention) | Existing procedure | (a) | Maintenance schedule |

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run 20 production cycles on the same furnace with the new coordinated schedule (Rows 2–6) vs 20 baseline cycles (historical or concurrent control). Same alloy, same braze specification.
Instruments: Existing furnace thermocouples (pack uniformity), existing rail deflection gauges or post-cycle CMM on rail positions, existing shield-short detection (hipot or resistance).
Pass/fail thresholds: (1) Rail deflection growth per cycle ≤30% of baseline rate (mm/cycle); (2) Pack temperature uniformity (max ΔT at soak) ≤ baseline +5°C; (3) Zero shield shorts in 20 cycles (baseline: ≥1 short per 10 cycles).
Duration: 20 cycles per arm (~2–3 weeks).
Kill criterion: If rail deflection growth per cycle >50% of baseline OR any shield short occurs, the intervention fails — revert to baseline and investigate.

PHYSICS_DIRECTION_UNSTATED: the answer must carry an explicit DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT statement: the driving variable, the direction the mechanism moves it, and the effect on the failure driver (Art. 25 direction-of-effect; the auditor judges whether the stated direction is correct)
